Rashi on Nedarim 23a:1:1.hebrew: והוו מצטערי רבנן - והיו נוסעים משמש לצל ומצל לשמש מרוב תוגה, שלא היו יודעין לומר דבר פתח לחרטתו:
Rashi on Nedarim 23a:1:1.english: And the Sages were troubled - And they were moving from sun to shade and from shade to sun out of great distress, because they did not know how to say anything [as] an opening for his regret.

Rashi on Nedarim 23a:4:1.english: With a launderer's tool - A vessel in which the launderers place their garments.

Rashi on Nedarim 23a:5:1.hebrew: אין פותחין בנולד - שאין ראוי ליארע כזה, אבל הני דאמרן דמצטערי רבנן לאו מילתא דנולד הוא:
Rashi on Nedarim 23a:5:1.english: We do not broach [dissolution] using a new situation - for such [a thing] is not likely to occur; however, these [cases] that we mentioned, where the Sages are troubled, are not a matter of a new situation.

Rashi on Nedarim 23a:5:2.hebrew: אמר ליה האי נמי שכיחי אפיקורי דמצערי רבנן - כי האי, ולא דמי לנולד:
Rashi on Nedarim 23a:5:2.english: He said to him: This too — heretics who trouble the Sages are common - like this [one], and it is not comparable to a new situation.

Rashi on Nedarim 23a:8:1.hebrew: ר"א בן יעקב אומר אף הרוצה להדיר את חבירו שיאכל - שאומר לו: "קונם שאין אתה נהנה לי אם לא תאכל עמי", היינו נמי נדרי זרוזין, שאינו מדירו אלא כדי לזרזו שיאכל עמו. יאמר: "כל נדר שאני עתיד לידור יהא בטל":
Rashi on Nedarim 23a:8:1.english: R. Eliezer ben Yaakov says: Even one who wants to subject his fellow to a vow so that he will eat [with him] - Where he says to him, "Konam that you may not benefit from me if you do not eat with me" — this too is [a case of] vows of incitement, for he only subjects him to the vow in order to urge him to eat with him. He should say, "Any vow that I will make in the future shall be void."

Rashi on Nedarim 23a:9:1.hebrew: לא שמע ליה - האי מודר, ולא אתי למיכל בהדיה, הואיל והנדר בטל:
Rashi on Nedarim 23a:9:1.english: He will not listen to him - [That is,] this one who is subject to the vow, and he will not come to eat with him, since the vow is void.
